title: The Almighty no one can reach, harm or defeat
subtitle: Al-Aziz: the Mighty whose honor is untouchable and who shares it with you
intro: Al-Aziz (الْعَزِيزُ) means The Almighty: the One who is overwhelming in strength, beyond the reach of any harm, never defeated, and the source of all honor. Whoever seeks dignity from Him is raised, and whoever seeks it from people or things is eventually let down. This name tells you where real worth comes from.

root.sense: The Arabs called hard, packed ground that rain cannot soak into ard 'azaz: a surface nothing gets through. From it come 'izza: strength, invulnerability and honor, and also rarity and preciousness. Picture the lead-lined door of an X-ray room: whatever tries to pass is stopped. Al-Aziz is the One nothing can penetrate, overcome or diminish.

row.title: Status comes from things
sub: the car, the title, the crowd

knowing: Scholars describe three layers in this name. {idea}He is mighty in strength, so nothing He wills fails; mighty in being beyond reach, so no creature can harm Him or add to Him; and mighty in prevailing, so every power in existence submits to His decree{/idea}. On top of this, the word carries preciousness: He is the One most dear, without equal or substitute.

Human might always has gaps. The strongest army has supply lines, the richest company has creditors, the fiercest ruler sleeps. Al-Aziz has none of these. He also does not abuse His might. The Quran pairs Al-Aziz with Al-Hakim, the Wise, more often than almost any other two names. Tyrants are mighty without wisdom, so they crush. {reward}Allah is mighty and wise: His strength always lands in the right place, at the right time, for the right reason.{/reward}

Al-Aziz is also distinct from Al-Qawiyy. Al-Qawiyy speaks of the strength itself; Al-Aziz speaks of what that strength produces: being unconquerable, untouchable and honored. One is the power, the other is the invincibility and dignity that come with it.
seeing: When Allah first spoke to Musa at the fire, on his way back to face the most powerful man on earth, He introduced Himself with these two names: It is I, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise (27:9). A frightened man with a stick needed to know that the One sending him could not be defeated, and that every hardship of his past had been placed with wisdom.

When Ibrahim left his people for an unknown land, with Lut beside him, he said he was emigrating to his Lord, the Almighty, the Wise (29:26). No army, no road map, only the knowledge that the One he travelled to could protect him on any road.

And on the night the Prophet ﷺ stood in prayer repeating a single verse until dawn, as reported by an-Nasa'i, it was this one: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise (5:118). His might is not only the might to punish. It is the might to forgive without anyone being able to object.
trusting: Much of our anxiety is about status: being looked down on, losing face, not being respected at work or in the family. Al-Aziz answers it directly. Whoever wants honor, all honor belongs to Allah (35:10). {trap}When dignity depends on a job title, a brand or other people's opinion, it can be taken in an afternoon.{/trap} When it comes from being His servant, nothing can strip it away.

It also gives courage when you feel small. The Quran says honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers (63:8). You do not need to hide your prayer, shrink your faith or apologize for your values to be worth something. {reward}Lean on Al-Aziz and you stand straight in any room, without arrogance and without fear.{/reward}
loving: We love strength that protects us and dignity that lifts us. Al-Aziz has both in perfection, and He does not hoard His honor. He shares it with anyone who turns to Him, even the poorest and most overlooked. {reward}The heart falls in love with a Mighty One who uses His might to forgive, to protect the weak, and to raise up those the world ignores.{/reward}
now: You are in a meeting and a colleague makes a joke about your fasting, and the room laughs. You feel your face burn. {idea}Remember whose honor you carry: it was never theirs to give or take.{/idea} You can smile, answer calmly, and walk out with your dignity whole.
old: My worth rises and falls with how people see me and what I own.
new: My honor comes from Al-Aziz, so no laugh, loss or title can take it away.
try: Next time you feel the urge to impress someone, pause and quietly say: honor belongs to Allah, then act as His servant rather than for their approval.

dua.text: Ya Aziz, You cannot be overcome and Your honor cannot be touched. Honor me with obedience to You, do not humiliate me through sin, and let me never seek dignity from anyone but You.
dua.note: Call on Al-Aziz when you feel weak, humiliated or outnumbered, and recall 5:118, where the Prophet ﷺ turned to this name to plead for forgiveness for his people.

pairs.why: The Quran's favorite pairing: Al-Aziz is unstoppable might, Al-Hakim makes sure that might is always used with perfect wisdom.
Often joined in the Quran (as in Surah ash-Shu'ara): His might never cancels His mercy, so the strongest is also the kindest.
Al-Qawiyy is the strength itself; Al-Aziz is the invincibility and honor that flow from it.

faq.a: Al-Aziz means The Almighty. It describes Allah as overwhelming in strength, beyond the reach of any harm, never defeated, and the source of all honor and dignity. The word also carries the sense of rare and precious: there is nothing like Him and nothing can replace Him.

faq.q: Why is Al-Aziz so often paired with Al-Hakim?
faq.a: Because might without wisdom becomes tyranny. Pairing Al-Aziz with Al-Hakim tells us Allah is not only unstoppable but also places every act of His power exactly where it belongs. His strength is never random, never excessive and never unjust.

faq.q: Can a person be called Aziz?
faq.a: Yes. The Quran uses aziz for people, such as the chief minister of Egypt in the story of Yusuf, and even describes the Prophet ﷺ as one to whom his people's suffering is grievous (9:128). What belongs to Allah alone is perfect and absolute might. People can be named Abdul Aziz, servant of the Almighty.

faq.q: How do I get honor according to Islam?
faq.a: The Quran says whoever wants honor should know that all honor belongs to Allah (35:10). Honor comes through faith, obedience, good words and righteous deeds, not wealth, lineage or brands. Seeking dignity from people tends to end in humiliation; seeking it from Al-Aziz lasts.
